title: Codecaine — Design your real app, not a picture of it
excerpt: Codecaine opens your running app on an infinite canvas. Design on its real elements, press Save, and your AI agent writes it into your code. Free, Mac and web.

Bring your code. in your canvas.

Run it. Remix it. Bring the whole internet into it. Your app, your references, your files, and your AI all meet on one infinite canvas. Experiment with anything. Build without breaking your flow.

Free forever · macOS and web · works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others

  • React
  • Next.js
  • Vite
  • Tailwind CSS
  • shadcn/ui
  • GitHub

How it works

Pick a project. Codecaine sets it up, runs it and puts it on the canvas. Then you edit the real thing.

01 · Pick a project

A folder on your Mac or a repo on GitHub – whatever you're already working on. Codecaine works out what it needs to run, and installs whatever's missing the first time. You don't configure anything. You don't read a setup guide. You definitely don't open a terminal “just to check something.”

02 · It runs on the canvas

Codecaine starts your project, opens it, and puts the running page on the canvas. Not a screenshot. Not a rebuild. Your actual app – router, data, and that loading spinner you keep meaning to fix.

03 · Edit anything

That's it. Click anything on the page and change it – the spacing, the type, the layout, the copy. Every change lands in your code. The handoff meeting has been cancelled. Indefinitely.

The web is your canvas.

Bring in a live website, a Figma frame, some code or a PDF. It lands on your canvas as layers you can edit.

Consistency, built in.

Set colours, spacing and type once, as variables. Use them everywhere, and change them all at once whenever inspiration strikes.

One canvas. Always in sync.

Design on the canvas and hit save. Your code on GitHub follows along with no extra commands, and if two changes collide, you pick the one that wins.

The design features you expect.

On the code you already have.

Your muscle memory still works.

The shortcuts you know from design tools work here too. No new habits, nothing to relearn.

Resize without the cleanup.

Scale a group and its text, strokes, corner radii and effects scale with it. Everything stays in proportion.

Get the spacing just right.

See the distances between elements as you work. Fine-tune spacing and alignment without guessing your way through pixels.

Layouts that move with you.

Auto layout on flex and grid, so a layout holds together when its content changes.

The details make the design.

Drop shadows, layer blur and background blur add the depth. Fine-tune the finish without leaving your canvas.

Color outside the lines.

Linear, radial and angular gradients, with layer masking, right on your canvas. Tune every blend until it feels like yours.

The fact, when everyone has access to the same tools, the things that make us different become even more important.

Your judgment. Your obsession with the small things. Your ability to recognise when something looks good but doesn't feel right.

Fair questions, straight answers.

Ready to try it? Setup is one command for your agent.

What is Codecaine?

A desktop design editor for code you already have. It opens your running project on an infinite canvas, lets you select and change its real elements with the controls of a design tool, and works with your AI agent to write those changes into your files.

Do I have to change my project to use it?

No. Open the folder: Codecaine installs it, starts its dev server and frames the running page. Nothing of the editor's goes in your project's root. The canvas keeps its own layers in a .codecaine folder inside the project.

Where do my changes go?

Into your code. What you change on the canvas waits in a list of changes. Save hands them to your AI agent, which writes them into the project's source. From there you commit, sync to GitHub and deploy the way you always do.

Which AI agents does it work with?

The one you already use. Setup installs and signs in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, opencode or Pi. Pick yours on the install page.

Can I start without a project?

Yes. Remix a site from the Community and it opens running, or import a webpage, a Figma frame, HTML, a PDF or a spreadsheet onto the canvas as layers.

What does it cost, and where does it run?

Nothing, and that's not a trial. Codecaine is free forever. It runs as a Mac app on Apple Silicon, and in your browser at web.codecainehq.com, where your agent connects over MCP.

Your product, on a canvas. Free forever.

Open your running project, change it like a designer, ship it like an engineer.

Perfection is achieved, not when there is nothing more to add, but when there is nothing left to take away.

PS: Everything is design. Everything!
